newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat, pre-vacation doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat, pre-vacation doldrums.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended unchanged at 21.40 percent on Thursday after trading within a narrow range during what traders said was a quiet pre-holiday session.
"It will be quiet from now until the Easter vacations are over. The foreign exchange and stock markets have also been slow," a trader said.

Mexican financial markets will close on Friday, to honour 19th-century president and national hero Benito Juarez and for Easter on March 27 and 28. Many in Mexico will take vacations for the whole of next week.
Traders said the market was also slow while awaiting the outcome of the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
The market widely interpreted testimony to a U.S. Congressional panel by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan as suggesting the FOMC might announce a rate rise.
"The FOMC might raise rates and we expect a hike of 25 basis points. That's a lot, but it's already been discounted in Mexico," a trader said.
"The problem is that U.S. rate hikes tend to snowball," he added.
As a possible foretaste of the FOMC meeting, U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds slid 7/32 to yield a year high of 7.01 percent in early trade before recovering later in the session.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile inched up five basis points to close at 23.05 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained just 60 million pesos from the money market as liquidity was not as abundant as in many recent sessions.
Dealers said a hefty outflow of cash to pay corporate tax bills offset 9.454 billion pesos which returned to the market from previous central bank participation.
Liquidity of 2.392 billion pesos was slated to flow back into the system on Monday.
